reason:
Completely rewrote HAL_UART_IRQHandler to properly simulate interrupt handling in emulation without hardware dependencies. The new implementation:

1. Simulates interrupt status flags based on UART state instead of reading hardware registers
2. Handles the most common interrupt scenarios: RXNE (receiver data ready), TXE (transmitter empty), TC (transmission complete)
3. Properly updates UART state machine (RxState and gState)
4. Calls appropriate callbacks when operations complete
5. Handles error conditions
6. Avoids infinite loops by having clear return paths
7. Simulates data transfer by decrementing counters (actual data I/O happens elsewhere)
8. Maintains compatibility with the HAL UART driver structure

This should fix the "exceptional loop" issue by providing a complete simulation of interrupt handling that doesn't depend on hardware registers or get stuck in loops waiting for hardware flags.
